topic: Motion, Waves, Sound, Light, Heat, and Electricity
key_concepts: Motion is a change in position from an initial to a final location.
Distance is the total length of the path traveled.
Displacement is the straight-line change from reference point to final point.
Distance and displacement are equal only for straight-line motion in one direction.
Scalar quantities have magnitude only; vector quantities have magnitude and direction.
Speed is distance divided by time.
Velocity is displacement divided by time and includes direction.
Waves are disturbances that transfer energy.
Sound waves have characteristics such as pitch and loudness.
Light travels in straight paths and can be separated into colors.
Heat transfers by conduction, convection, and radiation.
Conductors allow heat or electricity to flow; insulators resist flow.
